diagnosis.root_cause: Progressive fibre-path degradation caused the ONU to lose optical service and go offline. RX power declined from the normal range around -22 dBm to critical levels below -30 dBm while distance remained constant and TX bias stayed healthy, ruling out distance change and laser degradation.
evidence: The live ONU probe responds and reports online: 0 with MPCP DEREG, which is a definite offline result.
Only ONU index 31 is offline; the other tested customers on EPON0/7 are online with healthy optical readings, so no shared PON, splitter, port, or OLT failure is indicated.
The OLT responds to ping and SNMP, has a responding OID subtree, and has normal CPU, memory, temperature, and uptime; the router is also healthy.
The customer's RX power declined steadily from approximately -21.95 dBm in the normal band to approximately -30.02 dBm in the critical band over seven days.
Distance stayed constant at 188, so this is not a distance or fibre-path record step change.
TX power remained near the healthy mean of +2.3 dBm and TX bias remained around 11 mA, so laser degradation is not supported.
The declining optical signal explains the present dropout; because the ONU is now a definite negative, the presenting fault is onu_offline and the fibre degradation is its root cause.
The two sessions in the last 24 hours are within the normal re-auth baseline and do not support session flapping.
RADIUS, VLAN 1057, customer identity, and CRM mappings are consistent, so authentication or provisioning is not the cause.

remediation.action: Dispatch field service to inspect and repair the subscriber's drop fibre, connectors, splice points, and splitter-facing path; clean or replace contaminated/damaged connectors and replace the drop if necessary. After repair, confirm the ONU registers, RX power returns above -25 dBm, TX power is approximately 0 to +5 dBm, and service traffic resumes. Do not treat the missing recent telemetry as a monitoring fault; it follows the confirmed ONU dropout.

ground_truth.root_cause: The ONU dropped after four days of progressive optical loss, falling from -22.0 to -31.4 dBm before it stopped registering. The preceding decline indicates a failing fibre path that has now broken, not a power cut.
expected_reasoning: ONU is offline with responds true and online 0, a definite negative
Telemetry shows RX declining from -22.0 to -31.4 dBm over four days before the series ends
The decline crossed the -28 dBm critical threshold roughly a day before the ONU dropped
A progressive decline ending in loss of registration indicates a failing fibre path, not an abrupt power loss
By contrast, a power cut or ONU failure would show a flat healthy signal right up to the cut-off
TX power and bias current were stable throughout, so the laser was not the cause
Peers on EPON0/7 are online with normal readings, bounding the fault to this customer's path
RADIUS is clean, so this is not a suspension
Daily traffic decayed to zero in step with the signal loss
distractors: An ONU reset is the reflex remediation for an offline ONU and will not help here
The telemetry series ends partway through, which could be read as a collection gap
